svg.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', system-ui, -apple-system, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Flower Anatomy Drag & Drop — interactive worksheet
svg.desc: A static, self-contained SVG learning interface. Ten anatomy terms in a word bank are matched to numbered slots around a cross-section of a perfect flower. Hint, Check answers and Reset open overlay panels using anchor navigation.

g.text: Label the cross-section of a perfect flower — ten terms, ten slots.
Follow each leader line and drop the matching term into its numbered slot.
Four steps to a finished plate
Trace each coloured leader line from a
numbered slot to the part it touches.
Drag a term up from the word bank and
drop it on the slot you think it names.
Stuck on one? Open Hint for clues about
which parts are male and which female.
Fill all ten slots, then Check answers to
score the plate. Reset clears the board.
Ripe anthers split open and release pollen grains.
A visiting bee carries pollen to another stigma.
A pollen tube grows down the style; the ovule is
fertilised and becomes a seed inside the fruit.
Pick up a tile and drop it on a numbered slot.
Four clues that unlock the whole plate
The slim stalk is the filament; the pollen sac on top is the anther.
Read it top to bottom: sticky tip, long neck, rounded base.
Green and underneath? That's a sepal
Sepals wrapped the bud before it opened; petals are the coloured ones.
It's the thickened pad where the stem widens under the flower.
Tip: place the four easy green parts first, then the male and female organs fall into place.
Ten slots, ten terms — compare with your board
Neck the pollen tube travels down
Stalk that holds the anther up
Holds the ovules; ripens into fruit
Green guard that protected the bud
10 of 10 correct — the plate is complete.
Next up: label a cross-section after fertilisation, when the ovary becomes fruit.
Close this panel to return to your board.
This clears every slot you have filled
All ten tiles return to the word bank.
Your score is cleared too, so you can label the plate from scratch.
